label: D1 after an unrewarded common a2->S2 trial
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO or D2), and almost only when the reward input is 0. Within that, it is specific to the previous trial having been an a2 choice that reached S2 by a common transition and went unrewarded (the common-unrewarded outcome that should drive a switch away from a2). Dev P=0.93 R=0.79 F1=0.85. It essentially never fires after a reward, after a1 choices, or after rare transitions (prev_common==0 holds under 1% of mass). Most misses (about 16% of mass) are the first D1 of each window, where the previous trial is outside the window so prev_action/prev_common are unknown; there it fires at rew=0 mostly when the agent goes on to choose a2. Activations are larger when a2 has been chosen repeatedly in the preceding trials (top windows are runs of a2->S2c). The weakest activations come when the a2 choice followed a history of a1 choices. All predicate variables are observed at D1.

issues: The factual claims hold. The feature fires only at D1: GO and D2 have 0 active steps, and in_rew=1 has 23 active steps against 37718 at in_rew=0. prev_action=1 holds 0.7% of the activation mass and prev_common=0 holds 0.8%. The test scores reproduce: P 0.932, R 0.797, F1 0.859, mass recall 0.834. About 15.9% of the mass falls on the first D1 of a window (prev_action=-1), as the explanation says.

There is a systematic false-positive class: trials where the agent switches. Splitting the predicate by the agent's upcoming choice on test gives precision 0.997 and mass recall 0.796 when the agent repeats a2 (action==2), but precision 0.68 and mass recall only 0.038 when it switches to a1 (action==1). By count, about 2475 of the 2556 false positives are switch-to-a1 trials. All the false positives shown by the misses tool are D1s after an unrewarded a2->S2 common trial where the agent then chose a1.

So the explanation's framing that the outcome 'should drive a switch away from a2' runs against the data. The feature is strong when the agent is about to REPEAT a2 despite the common-unrewarded outcome, and weak or absent when it switches. The label leaves out this dependence on the agent's own upcoming choice, which is a legitimate input. The first-window rows that the explanation already noted point the same way: there it fires mostly when action==2.

The history effect on magnitude checks out with scores, not just by inspecting windows. With the trial two back being a2, precision is 0.96 and mass recall 0.65. With it being a1, precision is 0.65 and mass recall 0.02.

No predicate beat the original's test F1 of 0.859. Adding action==2 gives F1 0.808. Adding the first-window clause gives F1 0.849 with mass recall 0.984. Requiring action==2 or a2 two trials back gives F1 0.841. The predicate is therefore a good boundary, but the label and explanation misdescribe what the feature tracks within it.
skeptic.revised_label: D1 after an unrewarded common a2->S2 trial, mainly when the agent goes on to repeat a2 (strongest after runs of a2 choices; weak when the agent switches to a1)
